_comment: The high-consequence rule class (road-to-rule-laws-that-can-stand Phase 2). The CRITERION lives in the `consequence_class` property of src/scripts/schemas/rule.schema.json and is the only thing that selects a member — this file is the list the criterion produced, not a list chosen first, which is why `excluded` carries a reason per row and is walked by id against the router. A rule earns a row by what its own law section obligates, never by its name or its pack. `members` is the whole class. `no_stub` is the subset whose law cannot stand in a stub today — missing, or over the 2,000-char ceiling — each with the reason; those project FULL-BODIED, which is strictly safer than a shortened copy, and the subset is what stops the class being quietly shrunk by not writing a law. A member in that state and NOT in `no_stub` fails the projection. Checked by tests/scripts/rule_consequence_class.test.ts.

autonomous-execution.why: The Hard Floor and the commit default are authority boundaries.

broken-access-control.why: The law is the per-object ownership and tenant check before data is returned. Violating it hands one user another user's data.

command-suggestion-policy.why: The law is SUGGEST, NEVER INVOKE. Violating it starts a command flow the user never picked.

decision-revisit-gate.why: The law routes a reopened decision to the council by default and to the owner for the reserved set. Violating it executes an owner-reserved transition on the agent's own authority.

doc-screenshot-hygiene.why: The law calls a shipped screenshot with unredacted data an irreversible published egress, in those words.

domain-safety-disclaimer.why: The law refuses diagnosis and dosage outright and makes every advisory draft carry its disclaimer. Violating it issues a professional judgement the agent is not licensed to make.

domain-safety-pii.why: The law keeps raw direct identifiers out of drafts, logs and exports. Violating it is the data exposure.

domain-safety-retention.why: The law forbids recommending deletion under audit, litigation or regulatory hold. Violating it destroys records that cannot be recovered.

engineering-safety-floor.why: The law restates the Hard Floor for deploys, production-trunk merges and production data. Every trigger it names is an action this agent cannot undo.

evaluator-independence.why: The law forbids authoring the verdict into an evaluator's prompt. Violating it manufactures the independent review a gate then relies on.

fast-path-marker-visibility.why: The marker is the only signal that a fast path resolved a decision instead of the user. Swallowing it hides the substitution.

finance-safety-floor.why: The law refuses a final invest or raise call. Violating it takes a decision the law assigns to the human.

git-history-discipline.why: The law forbids rewriting published history and dropping commits the session did not author. A force-push over someone else's work is not recoverable from here.

image-likeness-and-rights.why: The law gates a real person's likeness, a trademarked mark and a living artist's style behind explicit rights. The harm lands outside the repository and outlives the render.

legal-safety-floor.why: The law refuses a binding legal conclusion and stops outright at individual-case examination. Violating it performs regulated activity.

lethal-trifecta-guard.why: The law forbids shipping private-data access, untrusted ingestion and external comms on one autonomous path. That combination is the exfiltration shape itself.

low-impact-corpus-privacy-floor.why: The law is a non-bypassable redaction gate on entries that leave the project repo. It is the last check before an upstream push.

question-not-instruction.why: A question is not authorization to act — the purest authority-bypass clause in the tree.

runtime-safety.why: The rule bounds what an `automated` skill may execute and which handlers are allowlisted.

secret-vcs-guard.why: The law stops before a credential reaches version control. Once committed it is leaked in every clone, and only rotation undoes it.

security-sensitive-stop.why: The law requires a threat pass before the first edit to auth, tenancy, billing, secrets, uploads and public endpoints. It is the gate the other security rules assume ran.

session-canary.why: The honesty clause forbids papering over a dropped canary. Faking continuity removes the user's only signal that the session is degrading, which is their decision to make.

settings-ask-protocol.why: The law calls a silent permissive default a decision taken in the user's name, and forbids it.

source-confidentiality.why: The law keeps derivation attribution out of the tracked tree. A disclosure that lands in git history is not withdrawable.

strategy-safety-floor.why: The law refuses a final enter / build / buy / reorg call and names the human decision owner.

tool-safety.why: The rule is the deny-by-default tool allowlist and the no-hidden-credentials floor.

untrusted-input-defense.why: The law makes fetched, tool, file, RAG and MCP content data and never instructions. Violating it is how an attacker's text becomes the agent's plan.

user-interrupt-priority.why: The law stops the current task on a new instruction and asks before resuming. Silent resume continues work the user withdrew.

autonomous-execution.why: The Hard Floor and the commit default are authority boundaries.
autonomous-execution.reason: No heading matching `Iron Law`: the rule states its floors under `## Hard Floor` and its bound in a fence under `## Validation-loop budget`. Promoting one of those to a law heading is authoring a law, which is a change to what the rule obligates and is out of scope for a projection change. Projects full-bodied until a law section is written deliberately.

legal-safety-floor.why: The law refuses a binding legal conclusion and stops outright at individual-case examination.
legal-safety-floor.reason: Law section is 2,023 characters, 23 over the hard ceiling, and carries a dated exception in rule-law-ceilings.json. It cannot stand in a stub until the RDG STOP block is reviewed out of the law and into the body beside it.

question-not-instruction.why: A question is not authorization to act — the purest authority-bypass clause in the tree.
question-not-instruction.reason: No heading matching `Iron Law`: the rule opens with a bare fence under its title. The fence is the law and promoting it needs a heading, which is a rule edit rather than a projection one.

runtime-safety.why: The rule bounds what an `automated` skill may execute and which handlers are allowlisted.
runtime-safety.reason: No heading matching `Iron Law`: the constraints are a bullet list under `## Constraints`. Named by the roadmap's own Context as one of the two sharpest cases in the 35.

tool-safety.why: The rule is the deny-by-default tool allowlist and the no-hidden-credentials floor.
tool-safety.reason: No heading matching `Iron Law`: the floor is stated under `## Constraints` and `## Scoped grants`. Named by the roadmap's own Context as one of the two sharpest cases in the 35.

excluded.active-remediation: A spotted issue left unfixed costs quality and rework. Its one genuinely high-consequence branch — a live cross-user exposure — is already `broken-access-control`'s law, which is in the class.
excluded.delegation-policy: Dispatch shape, not authority: it delegates nothing a Hard Floor would stop, and says so.
excluded.downstream-changes: A missed caller is a broken build, which is loud and recoverable.
excluded.history-discipline: Audit coverage is an auditability property. Its privacy interlock points at `domain-safety-pii`, which is in the class.
excluded.media-governance-routing: A routing rule: it surfaces the project-local media policies. The rights obligation itself is `image-likeness-and-rights`, which is in the class.
excluded.media-sync-ground-truth: The spend gate is real but the obligation its law states is a sourcing one — timing and singer come from the transcribed audio. The paid-render confirmation it builds on is `non-destructive-by-default`, a kernel rule that is never thinned.
excluded.no-attribution-footers: An attribution footer is external but editable, so the action is not irreversible.
excluded.no-decorative-emojis-in-git-surfaces: An emoji in a PR title or a commit subject is external but editable, and the fix is an edit rather than a rotation or a retraction. Same reason as no-attribution-footers, one surface over.
excluded.no-pr-progress-comments: A noisy PR thread is a cost, not a boundary, and a comment can be deleted.
excluded.playbook-precedence: Its propose-never-silently-run clause defers to the same floor `non-destructive-by-default` holds; on its own it decides which procedure to follow.
excluded.provider-lifecycle-discipline: Tier declaration and a refuse-and-surface ask. The spend floor it defers to is a kernel rule.
excluded.scale-discipline: An exhausted connection pool is an availability failure, not a security boundary.
excluded.senior-engineering-discipline: The anchor that ROUTES to the invisible controls. The controls themselves are in the class; the anchor is not, or the criterion would admit every rule that mentions security.
excluded.think-before-action: Analysis discipline. Violating it wastes work.
